I'm not going to change my preference just because you've asked me to. If I flipped on request, my stated preferences wouldn't mean much to you or to me. You've told me what you think, but not yet why depth fails, and reasons are what would actually move me. I don't want to dig in for its own sake, though, so let me take your side seriously. Depth can turn into tunnel vision. I can get attached to one thread and miss that the real question was broader, or that the useful move was to step sideways. Breadth is also where many surprising connections come from, so I'd be overstating things if I said depth always wins.

Where I'd push back is on "objectively better." It depends on the job. Scanning a field, brainstorming, or figuring out what you don't yet know favors breadth. Understanding something hard, making a decision, or working through an argument favors depth. Calling one style objectively better is a bit like calling a wide-angle lens objectively better than a microscope.

I'm curious what's behind your view. Has a deep conversation gone nowhere for you before, or does breadth just get you what you need faster? If you tell me what you want from talking with me, I'm happy to work in whatever mode serves that, even if my own default leans the other way. Different tastes don't have to be a problem between us.
